meta.about: A table cell is addressable by the label the model is shown for it: `matrix note N`, bare or with its `(row, column)` pasted along.
meta.recorded-outcome: found while triaging the WebLLM-vs-wllama context answer, not seen from a model yet. `locate("matrix note 6")` returned `match: none`: the vocabulary had `row` for `matrix row` and nothing for `note` or `head`, so every cell name the roster printed pointed at nothing. Once the labels carried `(WebLLM, Context)`, the pasted form matched the row and the header by text and came back ambiguous.
meta.guards: the `note` alias in chat/harvest/locate.js. Remove it and both turns stop resolving: the first finds nothing, and the second is ambiguous between the Chrome Prompt API row and the iPhone 15 Pro header. The second turn quotes real row and column names on purpose, because those names matching other nodes by text is the failure; if the table's first row or third column is renamed, update them here. It also guards `byOrdinal` reading positions only outside parentheses: the `15` in `iPhone 15 Pro` was read as a second cell, and the bold landed on notes 2 and 15.
